articleSummary: As of June 9, 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has escalated to 550 confirmed cases and 101 deaths, predominantly in Ituri and North Kivu provinces. Laboratory capacity in North Kivu is under pressure due to reagent shortages, resulting in many pending test results. Immediate global health responses are essential as the outbreak continues to spread.

This incident underscores the ongoing challenges in controlling ASF in Vietnam, as the illegal handling of diseased animals poses significant risks to both the livestock sector and public health.
